chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from his father who said:

I always complained about my eyes. Once I complained about it to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, and he said: "Shall I not teach you a supplication beneficial for your worldly life and your hereafter, and which will also treat the pain in your eye?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say after the dawn prayer and after the sunset prayer:

"O Allah, I beseech You by the right of Muhammad and his progeny upon You, to bless Muhammad and his progeny, and to bestow light upon my sight, and insight upon my faith, and certitude upon my heart, and sincerity upon my deeds, and safety upon my self, and abundance upon my sustenance, and grant me to be ever grateful to You as long as You keep me alive."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and his progeny, and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.إخلاص: Sincerity, devotion to God alone in one's actions
key_terms.دبر: After/following (a prayer), refers to the period immediately after the obligatory prayer
key_terms.دعاء: Supplication (du'a), a prayer addressed directly to God

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Sadiq teach for eye pain and spiritual blessings?
ai.summary: A companion complained of chronic eye pain to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who taught him a comprehensive supplication to be recited after the dawn and sunset prayers. The du'a asks God, by the right of the Prophet and his family, for seven blessings: light in one's eyes, insight in faith, certitude in the heart, sincerity in deeds, safety of the self, abundance in sustenance, and perpetual gratitude. This teaching situates physical healing within a broader framework of spiritual well-being.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmed ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad al-Ja’fi, from his father who said:

I always complained about my eyes. Once I complained about it to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, he said: "May I teach you a prayer, beneficial for your life here and hereafter? And which will also treat the pain in your eye?" I said: "Yes." He said: Say after morning and maghrib prayers:

"O Allah, I beseech You in the name of Muhammad and his progeny, to bless Muhammad and his progeny, and to bestow light upon my eyes and insight upon my faith, certitude upon my heart, sincerity upon my acts, security upon my self, abundance upon my subsistence; and grant me to be ever thankful to You as long as You keep me."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his progeny.
